body:
`fence()` caps content with `tail()`, keeping the LAST maxChars. That is correct and deliberate for logs — a build/gate/prosecution failure is at the END — and exactly backwards for a specification, whose opening carries the constraints. An over-cap spec silently loses its beginning and every downstream gate proceeds on the remainder with a clean exit. #1007 calls this a false green, and it is the sharper half of the problem: `coldstart` audits the surviving tail, finds it internally coherent, and can return ZERO GAPS for a ticket whose opening requirements no longer exist.

Reproduction from the issue (packages/core/lib/text.mjs:41):

    const CAP = 8000;
    const spec = 'CRITICAL CONSTRAINT AT TOP\n' + 'y'.repeat(CAP + 50);
    fence('SPEC', spec, CAP).includes('CRITICAL CONSTRAINT AT TOP');  // false

DECIDED — do not revisit: implement the issue's OPTION 1 (explicit bias). Option 2 (fail closed when a spec-shaped payload exceeds its cap) is NOT in scope; note it as a follow-up for the fleet path and move on.

CORE FREEZE: this is authorized. CONVENTIONS.md rule 2 as amended by #1011 says a defect in an existing core primitive is FIXED IN CORE, not worked around locally, and requires the fix to ship a regression test in packages/core/test/ naming the issue it closes. Do NOT fork fence() per package — that is the exact failure #1005 documented.

WHAT TO BUILD

1. packages/core/lib/text.mjs — `fence(label, content, maxChars, opts = {})` taking `opts.bias` of 'head' | 'tail', DEFAULTING TO 'tail' so every existing call site is unchanged by the signature alone.
2. Fail closed on a bad bias: an unrecognized value throws, the way maxChars already does. A silently-ignored typo ('start', 'front', 'HEAD') would reinstate the defect at a site that believed it had opted out.
3. The truncation marker must name the end it KEPT: 'showing first N of M chars' for head, 'showing last N of M chars' for tail. The marker is the only signal a model gets about what is missing; saying 'last' while keeping the first is worse than saying nothing.
4. packages/core/index.d.ts declares fence with three parameters (:327). Add the optional fourth or core's contract test fails.
5. Set `{ bias: 'head' }` at the SPEC-SHAPED sites, and ONLY these:
   - packages/fleet/lib/charters.mjs:66 — fence('SPEC', ticket.body, ...) — the issue calls this the sharpest case: the builder is told a truncated body is its complete specification
   - packages/coldstart/lib/prompt.mjs:53 — fence('TICKET', ticketToText(ticket), ...)
   - packages/parallax/lib/prompts.mjs:86 — ticket body for edge-contract readings
   - packages/autopilot/lib/triage.mjs:83 — GitHub issue title + body (the title is literally the first line)
   - packages/premortem/lib/prompt.mjs:22 — fence('SPEC', specContent, SPEC_MAX_CHARS). NOT in the issue's table because #1010 added it afterwards, but #1010 shipped it with a comment that names #1007 as the reason its opening sections are at risk. It is the most spec-shaped site in the repo. Include it.

6. LOG-SHAPED sites keep tail bias and must not be touched: packages/fleet/lib/scheduler.mjs:186,206,233,246 and packages/fleet/lib/charters.mjs:28,89 (prior-attempt dead ends). charters.mjs contains BOTH kinds, so it cannot be a rail — read those three call sites individually and leave :28 and :89 alone.

RAILS: packages/fleet/lib/scheduler.mjs, packages/consensus-fix/lib/prompt.mjs, packages/review-calibration/lib/judge.mjs. These are the pure log-shaped and one-line-field fences; if any appears edited, the change has leaked.

WRITE THE RED TESTS FIRST

packages/core/test/text.test.mjs (required by rule 2, beside the existing fence assertions):
  - the issue's exact reproduction: a head-biased fence over cap RETAINS its opening line and DROPS its tail
  - a tail-biased fence over cap still retains its end — the log contract, unchanged
  - omitting opts entirely is byte-for-byte identical to the current tail behaviour (the default is the compatibility contract)
  - the head marker says 'showing first N of M chars', the tail marker says 'showing last'
  - an unrecognized bias throws, and the message names the offending value
  - under-cap content is untouched and unmarked for BOTH biases
  - the fence tag stays a per-call nonce under both biases (do not regress #1005)

Per changed call site, one test proving the opening survives: a body/spec/issue over its own cap keeps its first line and the prompt contains it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every red test fails before the change and passes after.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0.
- `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs` exits 0 on the diff.
- A grep of every fence() call site in the repo is shown in the PR, classified head or tail, with the reason — the completeness sweep #1005 established.
title: core: give fence() an explicit head/tail bias so specs stop losing their opening (#1007)
